clue.text: Have a discussion about introduction of invasive plant

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so the discussion word wraps the selected letter

parts.note: to confer is to talk things over

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of invasive

explanation.surface: A group debates what to do about an invasive weed that has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Apt to forget half of list in manifest

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it, so the shortened list goes inside the word for manifest

parts.note: manifest means plain to see
the first two of the four letters of list

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful mislays half the items on their shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manifest' looks like a cargo list to go with 'list', but here it is the adjective meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oblivious is unaware or heedless of things, so likely to forget them.

clue.text: Counteract the effect of secret agent's return somewhat

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from right to left
somewhat means only part of something, so the answer is a stretch of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: read backwards, secret agent runs t-n-e-g-a-t-e-r-c-e-s, and six consecutive letters of that give the entry

explanation.surface: Undoing the damage done by a spy coming home, at least in part.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to nullify it, cancelling out its effect.

clue.text: Scene is mistakenly introducing 100 subjects

indicators.note: introducing something means bringing it inside, so the number goes into the rearranged letters
letters set down mistakenly are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the two words used as letters to rearrange
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A film scene shot with a hundred extras goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciences such as physics or biology are fields of study, the subjects of a school or university.

clue.text: Withdrawal of speech that could escalate conflict

definitions.text: Withdrawal of speech that could escalate conflict

parts.note: surface reading: a speech being retracted, perhaps by a politician
setter's reading: refusing to speak to someone, a sulk that tends to make a quarrel worse

explanation.surface: A politician retracting an inflammatory speech that might widen a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Withdrawal sounds like retracting what was said, but it is the act of withholding talk altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the habit of deliberately ignoring someone and refusing to talk to them after a disagreement.

clue.text: Hotel near Cambridge with no vacancies, naturally

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
AT ELY: the cathedral city of Ely lies a few miles from Cambridge
the words run together with no spaces between them

explanation.surface: A fully booked hotel close to Cambridge, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No vacancies' pretends to be about full rooms; it tells you to close the gaps in INN AT ELY. Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something innate is inborn, so doing a thing innately means doing it by nature.

clue.text: This score explicitly excludes choir

parts.note: the plainest way of excluding something is to say not
CH is a standard abbreviation for choir, as on organ stops

explanation.surface: A musical score that pointedly leaves out the choir part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like music, but it is a cut or mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut a line in it, and a notch is such a small cut or mark.

clue.text: Monarch once did career officer's commissions

parts.note: Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
to career is to rush along, so did career is ran
a Detective Sergeant, a police officer

explanation.surface: A former monarch who ran a career officer's business for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career officer' reads as a single job title; career is really a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task one is asked to do for another, which is exactly what an errand is.

clue.text: Boil lanced by doctor is serious

indicators.note: a lanced boil has something pushed into it, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: a boil is a painful sore
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A GP lancing a boil is no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor alongside DR and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombre person or mood is grave and gloomy, which is to say serious.

clue.text: Enduring word for hunger?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lasting a long time
second meaning read cryptically: a term for yearning is long

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: to long for something is to hunger for it, so the word long is a term for hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term means lasting or extending over a great stretch of time, so it describes something durable.

clue.text: Put the finishing touches to Evita's representation on flyer

indicators.note: a representation of a name is a new rendering of it, so its letters are rearranged
in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
the five letters of Evita rearranged

explanation.surface: Adding final touches to a poster of Evita for the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a leaflet but is the bird. Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to smarten something up with small finishing improvements.

clue.text: Haitian cooking doesn't use one bit of anchovy paste

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order
what a recipe doesn't use is left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: the word used as letters

indicators.note: one bit of a word, here its first, is a single letter taken from it

parts.note: the first letter of anchovy

explanation.surface: A Caribbean recipe for fish paste that leaves out the anchovy.
explanation.walkthrough: One A comes out of HAITIAN, and the remaining six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is a smooth paste made from ground sesame seeds, used in hummus.

clue.text: Reluctant to talk about appeal returning money

parts.note: re means concerning

indicators.note: something returning travels back, so the word for appeal is read right to left

parts.note: it means sex appeal
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: A shy fundraiser hesitates to speak about an appeal bringing cash back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person keeps their thoughts to themselves and is disinclined to speak.

clue.text: Transmission time chosen to accommodate constraints of audiences

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: to accommodate something is to make room for it inside

parts.note: elect as an adjective means chosen

indicators.note: constraints are the bounds or limits, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of audiences

explanation.surface: A broadcast slot picked to suit the limits of its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: Constraints are the edges that hem something in, which is why they point to a word's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A telecast is a programme sent out by television, a broadcast transmission.

clue.text: Intriguing woman supported by old Spanish gentleman

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supported by another stands above it, so the second comes after

parts.note: a caballer is an intriguer, one who plots as part of a cabal
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A scheming woman propped up by an elderly Spanish gent.
explanation.walkthrough: CABALLER is an old word, in Chambers, for a member of a cabal; the woman is that plotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish for a gentleman or knight, literally a horseman.

clue.text: Ladies' man from California briefly dated star

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its tail

parts.note: the state's postal abbreviation
dated means saw, as in went out with
a nova is a star that suddenly flares

explanation.surface: A Hollywood womaniser who had a brief fling with a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity but is the astronomical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the 18th-century Venetian seducer, gave his name to any man who chases women.

clue.text: Boldly face challenging aspect of departing flight's announcement?

parts.note: someone departing is going out
a flight of stairs; spoken, one stair sounds like a fixed look

explanation.surface: An airport announcement about a departing flight that seems to be challenging you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is a set of steps, not a plane. 'Challenging aspect' backs up the second half: a stare is a challenging look.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstare someone is to hold their gaze until they look away, facing them down boldly.

clue.text: Idealistic individual, up to a point, surprisingly ignores "opt out"

indicators.note: a surprising result is not in the expected order, so the letters are reshuffled
what is ignored is left out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the phrase used as letters
the three letters to drop; out signals they go

explanation.surface: An idealist who, only partly, refuses to opt out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopian is a visionary who believes in a perfect society, an idealist.

clue.text: Banishes changes omitting book's coarse material

indicators.note: whatever changes takes a new form, so its letters are rearranged
omitting means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: the word used as letters
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A rule banishing all changes except those in a book's rough draft.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a rough woven fabric of jute or hemp, known in America as burlap.

clue.text: Stock characters appearing in every novel?

definitions.text: Stock characters appearing in every novel?

parts.note: surface reading: clichéd figures, such as the brooding hero, that crop up in fiction
setter's reading: the standard set of letters that every book is written with

explanation.surface: A critic sighing that the same tired stereotypes turn up in every novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters means letters of writing here, not people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters used to write a language is its stock of written symbols, found in any book.

clue.text: I try and rush back for Polish food

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
to have a go is to try
to rip along is to rush

explanation.surface: Someone sampling a Polish dish and then dashing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the definition hides its capital: it is the nationality, not shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirogi are Polish dumplings stuffed with fillings such as potato, cheese or meat.

clue.text: Part of range found in North American prayers

definitions.note: plural, whereas the answer is one series of them

indicators.note: something found in another is located inside it

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
a range is a kitchen stove, and the oven is part of it

explanation.surface: Mountain-range churches in North America where people say prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests mountains; it is a cooking range, a large old-style kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine consecutive days.

clue.text: Remove backing for subsistence level

indicators.note: the backing of a word is its rear end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of subsistence
to rase, an old spelling of raze, is to level a building to the ground

explanation.surface: Taking away financial support set at subsistence level.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out or remove it entirely.

clue.text: Lecture on ethics is inspired by state of mind

indicators.note: what is inspired is breathed in, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: morale is the spirits or mood of a person or group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosophy talk whose content is shaped by the speaker's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecture on ethics' reads as a noun phrase, but it is a verb: to lecture about ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to preach about right and wrong, delivering a sermon on ethical behaviour.

clue.text: Revolutionary means of extracting oil with a single stone

indicators.note: a revolutionary thing turns over, so the first piece is written backwards

parts.note: an oil rig drills for oil
taken as written
sole means only or single

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking oil extraction method that needs only one stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol, also spelt girasole, is a fire opal, a gemstone that shows a glow when turned.

clue.text: Manager repeatedly uses such language!

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is written out twice in a row, one copy after the other
a string that uses something holds it within, so only an inner stretch is kept and its ends are dropped

parts.note: the word written twice; cut mana from the front and ager from the back

explanation.surface: A football boss with a famously foul mouth swears at the team again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints at swearing; the language is a national one.
explanation.definitionFit: German is the language of Germany, Austria and much of Switzerland, the language the doubled word contains.

clue.text: Lay to rest start of appeal by court and work together?

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the first letter of appeal
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A lawyer ending an appeal by the court so the parties cooperate.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act upon one another, communicating or working jointly.
